Georeference based on coordinates and coordinate reference system

Source: R/georef_coord.R
georef_coord.Rd

Turns the distinct locations of a survey into a point SpatVector, one point per location ID, ready for extract_*().

Usage

georef_coord(df, geom = NULL, crs = NULL, id = NULL)

Arguments

df

A data frame, typically from prepare_coord().

geom

character. The field names with the x and y coordinates of the points. Defaults to the columns recorded by prepare_coord().

crs

character. The coordinate reference system in one of the following formats: WKT/WKT2, :, or PROJ-string notation. See crs. Defaults to the recorded CRS, else "EPSG:4326".

id

Optional character string naming the column that identifies the units. When NULL, the recorded key, ID, or ID_adm_div is used.

Value

A SpatVector of points with one variable, the location identifier.

Details

After prepare_coord(), the coordinate columns are known and geom can be left out. Without a crs, the coordinates are taken as longitude and latitude on WGS 84 ("EPSG:4326"), which is announced.

See also

terra::vect

Examples

survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
georef_coord(coord)
#> Taking the coordinates as longitude and latitude in "EPSG:4326"; give `crs`
#> otherwise.
#> class       : SpatVector
#> geometry    : points
#> dimensions  : 12, 1  (geometries, attributes)
#> extent      : 30.2733, 30.8974, -0.8786, 0.1409  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> names       :                ID
#> type        :             <chr>
#> values      : 30.87620_-0.87860
#>               30.45000_-0.70280
#>               30.85840_-0.39050
#>               ...
